outcomes.description: Move the book behind the flower, including the requested relative depth ordering.

nodes.question: Compare the source and edited images to identify the same rose using multiple cues, then independently assess whether the book moved toward and is behind that rose.
nodes.criteria: First match the source rose to an edited-image flower using combined cues such as petal shape, coloration, stem, position, and surrounding context; allow substantial appearance changes and do not treat color mismatch or a different-looking flower alone as proof of absence. If identity cannot be reliably resolved, return unknown unless visible evidence independently establishes movement/progress or lack of it. Once matched, assess depth ordering separately: complete if the book is behind the matched rose; partial only if visible book movement is toward being behind it but the ordering is not achieved; absent if the book shows no movement toward that ordering, even if objects changed or moved unrelatedly. Return unknown if identity, movement, or depth evidence is insufficient to make these judgments.
nodes.binding: Target: the book. Reference: the single rose in the source image; track that same rose across images using multiple visual cues, allowing appearance changes. Requested relation: the book is behind the rose in depth.

program.checker_template: Execute exactly the supplied visual check on the source and edited images. Follow its saved binding, criteria and dependency evidence. Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). Confidence is your reported confidence in this check's observation, not a calibrated probability. A requested fulfillment check uses complete/partial/absent/unknown. A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.
